title: KAFKA-21280: Do not send stale bytes after a failed file read in SslTransportLayer.transferFrom
body:
`SslTransportLayer.transferFrom` clears `fileChannelBuffer` before
reading the next chunk of the file. When the read threw, or returned no
bytes, the buffer was left cleared rather than flipped, so it still
looked full of the previous chunk. If bytes had already been written in
the same call the `IOException` was swallowed, and the next call sent
the stale buffer as the contents of the position that could not be read:
a read error on the segment never surfaced, and the client received a
corrupt batch.

This flips the buffer whether or not the read succeeds, so that it holds
exactly what was read: nothing after a failed read or at the end of the
file. It also rethrows the `IOException` when bytes were already written
in the same call: the connection is closed on it anyway, and returning
the bytes written only delayed the error to the next call.
